elements.element: The post-termination obligations are triggered upon expiry.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause applies only after resignation or termination; it does not address expiry, and the supplied text does not demonstrate that expiry is impossible.

elements.element: The post-termination obligations are triggered upon termination.
elements.evidence: The transition and delivery obligations expressly apply after the effective date of termination.

elements.element: The Vendor must provide transition assistance.
elements.evidence: The Servicer must cooperate in an orderly transition and provide the transition assistance described in Section 7.5.

elements.element: Transition assistance must be available for up to 6 months.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause requires assistance for at least 90 days but does not guarantee availability for up to six months.

elements.element: Transition assistance is provided at the Vendor’s then-current rates.
elements.evidence: No then-current-rate standard is included. Instead, added subsection (c) requires the resigning or terminated Servicer to pay specified transition expenses.

elements.element: The Vendor must return Customer Data.
elements.evidence: In the adapted servicing context, the predecessor Servicer must deliver the Receivable Files and its maintained accounts and records to the Successor Servicer.

elements.element: Customer Data must be returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: The clause specifies no machine-readable or other required export format.

elements.element: Customer Data must be returned within 30 days.
elements.evidence: The added transition-assistance provision requires delivery of the Receivable Files and maintained accounts and records no later than 30 days after the effective date.

elements.element: The Vendor must delete Customer Data after returning it.
elements.evidence: No post-return deletion obligation is included.

elements.element: The Vendor must certify deletion of Customer Data after deletion.
elements.evidence: No deletion certification obligation is included.

elements.element: The post-termination obligations are triggered upon expiry.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause covers resignation and termination, but not expiry.

elements.element: The post-termination obligations are triggered upon termination.
elements.evidence: The assistance and delivery periods run from the effective date of termination.

elements.element: The Vendor must provide transition assistance.
elements.evidence: The Servicer is expressly required to provide the transition assistance described in Section 7.5.

elements.element: Transition assistance must be available for 90 days.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause requires transition assistance for at least 90 days after the effective date of resignation or termination.

elements.element: The Vendor must export Customer Data.
elements.evidence: The predecessor Servicer must deliver the Receivable Files and its maintained accounts and records to the Successor Servicer, which functions as the required data export in this servicing context.

elements.element: Customer Data must be exported within 30 days.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause requires delivery of the specified files and records no later than 30 days after the effective date.

result.reason: The operative language implements the fallback durations for resignation or termination, but omits expiry as a required trigger, so the fallback is not completely satisfied. It also lacks the preferred six-month availability, then-current rates, machine-readable format, deletion, and deletion certification. The redline is not minimal and does not preserve unrelated commercial terms because it adds subsection (c), imposing a broad transition-expense reimbursement obligation on the resigning or terminated Servicer that neither position requires. Drafting quality is also reduced by the dangling source text and the unnumbered transition-assistance heading.
